title: Refactor ranking request model, cursor semantics, and candidate metadata
creator: Liam Chen
description: Goal: Improve ergonomics and scalability of the Reranking endpoint (inputs, top_k semantics, structured output, and pagination) to reduce client-side complexity, support stable paging across score ties, and unlock server-side batching/early-exit optimizations. This ticket scopes schema changes, compatibility rules, server-side implementation approach, benchmarks, migration plan, and rollout steps.
acceptance_criteria: New request/response schema specified and documented in the API spec (backwards-compatible extension path available)
Top_k semantics defined: deterministic selection, clear behavior on ties, and explicit max_results vs. page_size distinction
Cursor format that is opaque to clients but includes replayable state (last_score, last_index, model_version) and is stable across small scoring changes
Server implements structured per-candidate metadata (original_index, score, provenance tags) and optional explain vectors without inflating default response size
Benchmarks demonstrate <=1.5x latency regression (ideally improvement) for common sizes (top_k 10/50) and batch-friendly behavior for concurrent requests
Migration guide and SDK patching examples provided for JS/Python clients
Feature gated rollout with monitoring (latency, correctness, regression tests) and automatic rollback hooks
design_notes: Input schema: accept candidates as either text+id or precomputed embeddings; canonical candidate object: {id?:string, text?:string, embedding?:base64, metadata?:map<string>}. Prefer explicit id for stable provenance.

top_k semantics: separate 'max_results' (how many final candidates to return overall) from 'page_size' (how many candidates to return in this response). Backend guarantees deterministic selection by sorting on (score desc, original_index asc) before applying pagination window.

Cursor token: base64url-encoded JSON with fields {model_version, cutoff_score, last_original_index, tie_resolver_seed}. Token is opaque; server validates model_version to avoid mixing scoring rules across rollouts.

Structured output: response includes 'candidates' array where each element contains {id, score, rank, original_index, provenance: [tags], explain_vector?: optional compressed floats}. Explain_vector excluded by default and opt-in via parameter 'include_explain'.

Backwards compatibility: Keep current top_k param supported but deprecated; if both legacy and new params present, new params take precedence. Server returns a warning header when legacy params detected.
Performance: Introduce early-exit heuristics (score thresholding) and two-pass re-ranking: cheap approximate scorer -> select N' candidates -> full scorer. Design allows N' configured per route.
Streaming support: API supports chunked candidate pages for very large result sets. Streaming uses same cursor model; server must include final_cursor when stream ends.
Security: Cursor includes no PII; embedding data is only referenced by id in cursor to avoid leaking content in tokens. Note: still requires review for on-prem encryption policies.
tradeoffs: Opaque cursor vs. readable: Opaque tokens prevent clients from relying on internals but make debugging harder. Chosen opaque + server error codes + debug flag for playground.
Explain vectors optional: including them by default increases payload size and latency. Opt-in keeps common path small while enabling debugging and evals.
Deterministic tie-breaking by original_index relies on stable candidate ordering from caller; if caller sends unordered batches, they must supply stable ids to get stable paging.

Two-pass ranking adds complexity in runtime but yields large latency savings at scale; acceptable trade for Dedicated and Hosted tiers but we provide a fallback full-rerank mode for strict accuracy customers.
Deprecating legacy params increases migration cost for clients; we provide server-side compatibility and warnings to smooth the transition.
implementation_plan: Spec: finalize API schema doc and example payloads (3 days)
Spike: implement prototype two-pass reranker in sandbox service (5 days)
Server: implement cursor encoding/decoding, deterministic windowing, structured output fields (7 days)
SDK: add client helpers to create stable candidate lists and unpack cursor (JS+Python) (4 days)
E2E tests: add correctness tests for tie scenarios and cross-model-version behavior (3 days)
Perf: run benchmarks at scale and tune N' and batching thresholds (4 days)
Docs & Migration: write migration guide, update API reference and examples (3 days)
Rollout: feature flag + canary + rollout to hosted customers then Dedicated (2 weeks gating)
Total: staged across two sprints; break into sub-issues for parallel work
migration_plan: Compatibility mode: server accepts legacy top_k and page cursor but sets 'warning' header when used; automatic mapping to new params when possible
SDK patch: client helper to compute 'original_index' and to call 'stable_candidates' helper to produce deterministic ordering
FAQ for customers: describe differences between old and new paging behavior, provide conversion script to map offsets to cursors for simple cases
Rollout steps: enable new schema under flag for internal traffic, run integration tests with top customer workloads, invite 2 pilot customers (from CS) for early opt-in
Fallback: if cursor validation fails due to model_version mismatch, return HTTP 409 with instructions to restart query from page 0
Deprecation window: keep legacy params for 6 months after GA with automatic warning emails to active API keys
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): feature-flagged rollout for infra team + internal apps (1 week)
Phase 1 (canary): 5% traffic on hosted API with telemetry on p99/p50 latency, correctness diffs vs. baseline, and cursor failures (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (pilot customers): enable for selected customers who opt-in; gather feedback on cursor ergonomics and SDK UX (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (GA): Gradual ramp to 100% once monitoring thresholds met and SDKs released; announce deprecation timeline for legacy params
Rollback: implement automated rollback if >0.5% cursor failure rate or >20% tail-latency regression over baseline
testing_plan: Unit tests: cursor encode/decode, deterministic selection, tie behavior, explain vector serialization
Integration tests: cross-version cursor reuse, model fallback, streaming pages correctness
Load tests: synthetic workload with 10k QPS and varying candidate set sizes (10/50/200) to measure memory usage and latency
Chaos tests: introduce partial availability of full scorer and validate graceful fallback to approximate path
Regression tests: compare rank order with golden dataset used by evals team to ensure quality targets met
progress_updates: 2025-11-06: Ticket created after design sync with PM and Design; agreed to separate max_results vs page_size and to adopt opaque cursors.

2025-11-10: Spike completed; prototype two-pass flow reduces mean latency for 50 candidates from ~180ms to ~70ms in sandbox when batching is enabled (batch size 32). SNR of ranking preserved on 95% of queries.

2025-11-13: Schema draft v1 posted to Confluence and early SDK stub created (see links). Feedback from FE/SDK: include client helper for generating stable original_index when clients stream candidates.
2025-11-17: Implemented initial cursor encode/decode; discovered cursor must include model_version to prevent mixing scoring logic across rollouts — added to spec.

2025-11-20: Started server-side implementation for deterministic windowing and structured output. Benchmarks in CI show slight increase in median latency (5-10ms) but 2x-3x p99 improvement under concurrency due to batching gains.
Next: finish SDK integrations and prepare canary toggle
reviews: Security review: prelim notes added to security queue; on-prem KMS implications flagged for SRE review
